prompt: Explain why bonding is better described as a continuum than as three separate types.
markscheme: Most bonds have partial ionic and partial covalent character, depending on the electronegativity difference; e.g. AlCl₃ is not purely ionic **(R1)**. The bonding triangle places compounds between the ionic, covalent and metallic extremes **(A1)**

prompt: A compound's two elements have average electronegativity 2.6 and electronegativity difference 0.4. Predict its predominant bonding type and explain.
markscheme: Predominantly covalent **(A1)** — a small difference means little ionic character, and a high average electronegativity means both elements are non-metals, not metallic **(R1)**

prompt: Explain why an alloy such as steel is harder than pure iron.
markscheme: Atoms of different sizes (e.g. carbon) disrupt the regular lattice **(R1)**, so layers cannot slide past each other as easily **(R1)**

options: A mixture of different small molecules
A large molecule made from many repeating monomer units
A substance with an ionic lattice
markscheme: **B.** A macromolecule made of many repeating units derived from monomers.

prompt: Draw (describe) the repeating unit of poly(chloroethene) formed from CH₂=CHCl, and state what happens to the double bond.
markscheme: Repeating unit: –CH₂–CHCl– with continuation bonds at each end **(A1)**; the C=C double bond breaks (the π bond opens) so each monomer joins two neighbours; no other product forms **(A1)**

prompt: Explain how a polyamide forms from a diamine and a dicarboxylic acid, and name the small molecule released.
markscheme: The –NH₂ group of one monomer reacts with the –COOH group of another, forming an amide link –CONH– **(A1)**; a water molecule is released at each link **(A1)**
